description: An equation uses the equality sign and an expression does not - that one mark is the whole difference. In an equation the values on the left-hand side and the right-hand side are equal, but only for certain values of the variable, and those values are its solutions.

topic: What Makes an Equation Linear in One Variable
description: Linear means the highest power of the variable appearing in the expression is 1, so 2x, 3y - 7 and 12 - 5z qualify. Restricting to a single variable as well gives linear equations in one variable - the type studied since the earlier classes.

The two sides are assumed balanced, so the same operation performed on both leaves the balance undisturbed, and those steps give the solution. A solution is checked by substituting: x = 5 satisfies 2x - 3 = 7 while x = 10 does not.

Until now the right-hand side has usually been just a number, but it need not be - 2x - 3 = x + 2 carries a variable on each side. Subtracting x from both sides works because variables are numbers too, and that is the same thing as transposing x to the left.
concepts: Subtracting a term, not a number

description: An equation with fractions is multiplied through by the LCM of the denominators to clear them, then brackets are opened and terms transposed. Some equations are not linear to begin with but can be brought to linear form by multiplying both sides by a suitable expression.
concepts: Multiply by the LCM of the denominators
Check the answer against both sides
